key_insight: Single-crystal Ti-15Mo shows a surprising inversion of expected cubic elastic anisotropy: orientations near ⟨111⟩ are the softest in both modulus and yield onset, but hardness does not follow the same trend.
engineering_relevance: Texture and grain orientation can strongly alter local stiffness and first-yield behavior in β-Ti components, so constitutive models and process design must account for orientation-dependent nano-mechanics beyond simple Schmid/CRSS rules.
method: EBSD was used to identify crystal orientations near ⟨111⟩, ⟨124⟩, ⟨011⟩, ⟨023⟩, and ⟨013⟩.
Nanoindentation measured indentation modulus, hardness, yield onset, and strain-rate sensitivity on single-crystal regions.
Strain-rate-jump testing was used to estimate activation volumes and infer deformation mechanism changes.
evidence_signal: Across the tested orientations, modulus varied by about 10%, yield onset by 41%, hardness by 6.6%, and activation volumes of 18–31 b^3 supported kink-pair-nucleation-controlled plasticity.
watch_item: The proposed retained athermal ω explanation is plausible but indirect, so phase-specific evidence is needed before using it as a definitive mechanism in models.
paper_title: Orientation-Resolved Nanoindentation of Single Crystal Ti-15Mo: Inverted Elastic Anisotropy and Yield-Onset Behavior Beyond Simple CRSS Predictions
